page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance of the Intel Xeon processor is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression tests, both falling into the bottom 25% of benchmarks. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all registering in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests, including cached and uncached reads and uncached writes, also perform within the average range.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c6.6xlarge is its modest single-threaded processing speed, which may limit performance in single-core bound applications. However, its dedicated CPU allocation and 24 vCPUs provide stable multi-threaded execution. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a resource-dense option for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and general multi-core batch processing.
